name: Disodium lauroamphodiacetate
description: Disodium lauroamphodiacetate (CAS 14350-97-1 ), commercially known as Miranol H 2M, is an amphoteric surfactant derived from lauric acid used across personal care formulations. It functions as a mild cleansing, foam-boosting, and conditioning agent compatible with a broad range of ionic surfactant systems. In shampoos and body washes, it enhances foam volume and creaminess. This surfactant reduces the irritation potential of harsher anionic surfactants like sodium lauryl sulfate. Baby care and sensitive-skin cleansers rely on it specifically for its mildness profile. It supports effective cleansing without compromising skin or eye tolerance in delicate applications. Facial cleansers and micellar formulations use it to improve emulsification of sebum and light makeup residues. It also appears in conditioning shampoos and 2-in-1 formats, where its amphoteric character contributes to post-rinse softness. This versatility makes it a staple in modern cosmetic chemistry. Disodium lauroamphodiacetate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content commonly around 39–40%. It is available in cosmetic/personal care grade meeting industry standards. Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial-scale production.
